tldr: LACUNA is a programming model for LLM agents in which each action is a typed hole filled with model-written code that is compiled and type-checked against the surrounding program before execution, preventing unsafe or partially executed actions.
contributions: A code-as-action model where LLMs write agent actions as code running within their own runtime and checked at the call site before execution
A safety analysis providing pre-execution rejection of unavailable names and type mismatches, no partial execution of rejected snippets, and permissions/information-flow control
A demonstration that nested agent calls and ordinary code express common agent patterns (ReAct loops, skills, multimodel planning) as ordinary program control flow
A Scala 3 realization and evaluation on verifier test cases, BrowseComp-Plus, and τ²-bench
methods: The authors implement LACUNA in Scala 3, using its ability to compile a fresh snippet within the surrounding program's lexical context and track resource usage. Each agent action is a typed call agent[T](task) where the LLM receives the prompt, expected type T, enclosing source, and available names, then returns Scala code. The host compiler typechecks the generated snippet against T before any execution; if rejected, compiler diagnostics are fed back to drive retries. They also evaluate the system on BrowseComp-Plus and τ²-bench benchmarks.
results: On BrowseComp-Plus, 8.6% of generations are rejected before execution, with 0.7 retries per query on average, and the agent reaches 27.1% accuracy. On τ²-bench, LACUNA solves 76.0% of 392 tasks across four domains with a capable model, on par with the baseline agent.
limitations: Nested agent calls have no static bound on recursion depth; an accidental infinite recursion can look identical to a genuinely complex task from the outside. The runtime tracks depth with a configurable cap that throws an exception when hit. Additionally, a try block around an outer agent call catches compile failures from any nested agent call inside its snippet, even unrelated ones.
